nodes.summary: For maps `S P : V → V` there is an edge `x → y` exactly when `S x = y` and `P y = x` (Daskalakis, Goldberg and Papadimitriou, SIAM J. Comput. 2009, Section 3.1). Every vertex has at most one out-neighbour (`S x`) and at most one in-neighbour (`P x`).
nodes.title: The END-OF-THE-LINE graph

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `exists_solution`, some vertex `x` has `P (S x) ≠ x`, that is, has no outgoing edge (`forall_not_adj_iff`). Proof: otherwise `P ∘ S = id`, so `S` is injective, hence surjective on the finite set `V`; then `o = S y` gives `y = P o = o` and `S o = o`, a contradiction. This is the parity lemma "a directed graph with in- and out-degrees at most one that has a source has a sink" quoted in…
nodes.title: Every END-OF-THE-LINE instance has a sink

nodes.summary: Let `V` be finite and `S P : V → V` with a standard vertex `o` satisfying `P o = o ≠ S o` (so `o` is a source with an outgoing edge to `S o` whenever `P (S o) = o`). Then some `x` satisfies `P (S x) ≠ x` (a sink) or `S (P x) ≠ x` with `x ≠ o` (a source other than `o`).
nodes.title: END-OF-THE-LINE is total

nodes.summary: A vertex `x` has no outgoing edge if and only if `P (S x) ≠ x`.
nodes.title: Sinks of the END-OF-THE-LINE graph

nodes.summary: A vertex `x` has no incoming edge if and only if `S (P x) ≠ x`.
nodes.title: Sources of the END-OF-THE-LINE graph

nodes.summary: In the END-OF-THE-LINE graph two in-neighbours of a vertex coincide: both equal `P x`.
nodes.title: In-degree at most one

nodes.summary: In the END-OF-THE-LINE graph two out-neighbours of a vertex coincide: both equal `S x`.
nodes.title: Out-degree at most one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
